## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which a Crown's cart brings up the made road a printed sheet that is not the roll and does not go over it, and about four people in nine counties find out inside nine seconds that it is the best offer anybody in this county has ever been made, and three people who are not him give three more incompatible answers out loud in one street in one week, and none of the three is a refusal of the offer and all three are refusals of something else, and the roll is still on the boards with nine empty lines on all three copies and the fourth line empty on all three and nobody fills it and nobody takes it down.** It is also the block that spends two of the volume's six names, that puts five things on one board instead of the four that were on it at `chapter-0800.md`, that begins this county's own copy of a paper nobody can seal, and that leaves the low room at the back of that office shut and the drawer in it shut and the seal still in it.

`outline/volume-17.md` §8 Block 1 and §9 and §10 are binding and are not softened by anything in this file. `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 row is fixed. `outline/ending.md` is fixed. **DO NOT MOVE THE ENDING. DO NOT INTRODUCE A NEW FINAL ENEMY. THE ANTAGONIST IS THE SAME MAN HE HAS BEEN FOR SIXTEEN VOLUMES AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME PUTS HIM IN A ROOM.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE OFFER ARRIVES IN THE ORDINARY POST AND IT IS NOT THE ROLL AND IT IS NOT AN ORDER.** A Crown's cart comes up the made road with a printed sheet in it, the driver does not know what it is carrying, and the sheet asks for **the name of one person** to stand against the roads of nine counties, says in two sentences under the Marshal's hand that the place is being held to prevent a repeat of the Sundering, and **carries a date about nine weeks off the day it is nailed up.** **IT IS NAILED UP BESIDE THE THREE COPIES OF THE ROLL AND NOT OVER THEM, and the count of things on that board goes to five and the count of questions on it goes to three, and the page says so.** **THE FOUR ON THOSE BOARDS AT `chapter-0800.md` WERE ONE PRINTED NOTICE UNDER THREE COPIES OF A ROLL, AND THAT IS THE COUNT THE BLOCK STARTS FROM AND NOT THREE, and the second question was the roll's own and the third is the offer's.** **THE FOURTH LINE OF THE ROLL IS EMPTY ON ALL THREE COPIES AT THE BLOCK'S LAST DATELINE AND THE BLOCK MAY NOT FILL IT, MAY NOT PUT A NAME AGAINST ANY ROAD ON ANY PAPER, MAY NOT SHUT A ROAD ON THE STRENGTH OF ANY PAPER, MAY NOT TAKE ANY OF THE THREE COPIES DOWN AND MAY NOT TEAR ONE UP.**

**ABOUT FOUR PEOPLE IN NINE COUNTIES FIND OUT INSIDE NINE SECONDS THAT IT IS THE BEST OFFER ANYBODY IN THIS COUNTY HAS EVER BEEN MADE, AND FIVE HAD NOT, AND THE PAGE SAYS IT IN THE HOUSE'S CENSUS FORM.** **THE SCOPE OF THAT SUPERLATIVE IS THIS COUNTY AND NOT NINE COUNTIES, and the reason is on the page and is not pedantry: a person standing in a market street in this county is the only kind of person who can honestly have heard every offer this county has ever been made, so HERE in this block's title means THIS COUNTY and is the same claim. NO CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK MAY PRINT THE SUPERLATIVE OVER ANY WIDER SCOPE, AND A CHARACTER MAY NOT MAKE THE CLAIM ABOUT ANYWHERE HE HAS NOT LIVED.** **A CHARACTER WHO AGREES WITH THEM SAYS SO ONCE, OUT LOUD, IN HIS OWN TRADE, TO ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, AND IS NOT ARGUED WITH, AND ABOUT NINE HUNDRED PEOPLE ALONG ELEVEN MILES OF MADE ROAD HAVE NOT HEARD IT.** **Nobody in nine counties is argued out of it and nobody in nine counties is argued into it, and the volume does not decide who is right, because the sheet is true in its facts and false in its consent and both of those are on the page.**

**THREE MORE INCOMPATIBLE ANSWERS GIVEN OUT LOUD IN ONE STREET IN ONE WEEK BY THREE PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT HIM, AND NONE OF THE THREE IS A REFUSAL OF THE OFFER.** **Volume 16's three answers are not given a second time and this block may not merge them with these three, and may not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or a fourth voice of any of the six, and he says nothing out loud about any of them.** **The three trades are the block's own and must be different from Volume 16's three: Volume 16 gave a lime-keeper, a lime carrier and a keeper of records, and a Block 0001 writer chooses three of the following four and may not choose two of them.** **The woman who keeps a lime kiln and a stone-walled yard four miles north WAS IN THIS POOL AND IS WITHDRAWN FROM IT, being that she is Brida Lenth and she gave Volume 16's first of the three answers at `state/open-threads.md` 731 on day 2831 in thirty-one words, and a trade that has already given an answer to a different paper may not give one to this one.** The four that remain: a carter about thirty-eight who has driven up that made road about nine times and stopped at those boards four of them; **a woman of about thirty-nine who keeps a bindle and does other people's washing at the low end of that street and has a mouth on her and about nine people have already said she should not be asked anything**; a man of about forty-four who turns hurdles and hurdle rails and made four hundred of them in his life; a young man of about nineteen who keeps five frames of brood under about nine straw skirts and has said out loud twice that he will make no more bees than the bees he has got. **`Bessie Dellow`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Brida Lenth`, `Wyn Fell`, `Abel Chinn` and `Renn Ottery` are returns and cost nothing and any of them may give one of the three, and the first rule of this paragraph still governs whichever of them is chosen, being that a trade that has already given Volume 16 one of its three answers may not give one of this block's three.**

**THE TWO NAMES THIS BLOCK SPENDS, AND IT SPENDS EXACTLY TWO OF THE VOLUME'S SIX AND FOUR ARE HELD.** `Aren Kest`, `Mara Vey`, `Tovan Kest`, `Sera Quen`, `Hester Vane`, `Orme Skell`, `Dav Rundle`, `Tarr Lyster`, `Corve Sallow`, `Renn Ottery`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Wyn Fell`, `Abel Chinn`, `Brida Lenth` and `Bessie Dellow` are returns and cost nothing. **`Sabra Rolf` and `Gallow` may not be used for a new first name, and neither may `Iven` and `Marrow`, and neither may `Renn` or `Ost` as a surname, and neither may any first name or surname already printed in the hundred files from Chapter 701 onward.**

**THE NAME IS GIVEN THE WAY EVERYTHING IN THIS COUNTY GIVES A NAME, being that somebody asks one question about the person's own trade, kindly, at the low end of that market street, and the person answers, and then somebody asks what to call them because they want to know who to ask a second time.** **A name is not a promotion and a named person is not a leader and no chapter of this block gives either of the two an office, a rule, a vote, or a sentence in front of about four hundred people.**

**THE BLOCK'S RELATIONSHIP WORK IS NOT DONE HERE AND THE HOUSE SAYS SO ON THE PAGE.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 relationship work is separating the symbol from the partner, and `outline/volume-17.md` §8 Block 1 says Block 0001 does not do it. **So: nothing about the two of them is in any document, the word is not printed, nobody comments, nobody is thanked, the four and a half years are never described as four and a half years about the two of them, and no chapter of this block ends on the two of them.** At most this block puts one small ordinary thing on the page about a lamp at the foot of thirteen stairs and about who lit it and about who did not, and **the second lamp at the foot of those stairs is lit at the fourth hour on every one of the five mornings this block carries and it is not carried down any stair and it is not put in the middle of anybody's work, because Block 0003 spends that and the block that spends it must be the block that does it.** The legal form stays deferred to Volume 18.

**THE COST OF THE BLOCK IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT CURED IN IT.** The leg, which takes eleven miles in four hours before light and about nine otherwise and is worse than it was at the close of Volume 16; the ear on the side the stick is on, which is permanent and is the side she spoke from and which he turns his head away from on purpose; the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him; **and the bleed, which is fifty-one days old on this block's first dateline and ninety-two on its last and has not faded by anything anybody has done to it, which nobody in nine counties has asked him about, which is in no document, which has never been said out loud in a room, and which gets no panel and no explanation and no panel-shaped paragraph in any of these ten files.** **The scar is four hundred and thirty-two days old at the block's last dateline and is not cured and is not going to close over. The ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start in this block, and the mallet is not picked up, and the ninth thing is still shut by nine hurdles put there by the people at the end of it who would like them to stay.**

**THE ONE SYSTEM PANEL IN THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 17 IS RESERVED FOR BLOCK 0003 AND IS NOT SPENT IN THIS BLOCK. These ten files print no panel and no panel-shaped paragraph, and a panel here is a panel spent on nothing.**

**THE ANTAGONIST'S NAME IS PRINTED ZERO TIMES IN THIS BLOCK AND ZERO TIMES IN THIS VOLUME AND IS NEVER TO BE PRINTED AGAIN IN THIS PROJECT.** Volume 16's two printings at `chapter-0781.md` and `chapter-0797.md` were both documents and both are spent. Refer to him and to his instrument as *that notice*, *the Marshal's hand*, *the sheet*, *the offer*, *the warrant* or *the people with the warrant*.

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, not a cliffhanger cut in the middle of a sentence.** The sheet is on the boards beside three copies of a roll and the fourth line is empty on all three and the roll is not filled in and not taken down. **The county's own copy of the hand paper has been begun and has nine lines on it and no name on any of them and a trade on each, and the block's finding is that nobody can put a name on a line and everybody can put a trade on one, and that a line with a trade on it is a line somebody can be argued with.** The four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. The register holds ten questions and gains no entry and gains none in this block, and no fifth head is ruled, and the day-book stands at eleven entries on all ten datelines, and the leaf at the back of it carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody. **The low room at the back of that office is not entered in this block and the drawer in it is not opened and the seal is still in it, and nobody is asked what a seal is for.**

**`outline/volume-17.md` §16 item 6's three promises are CARRIED INTO BLOCK 0002 UNCONDUCTED AND NONE OF THEM IS BROKEN HERE:** no chapter of this block enters the Gatehouse or puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones; no consent of any sealed community is obtained, asked for, received or inferred, and the half leaf stays face down and no head is filled or ruled; and the roll is not filled, no name goes against any road, no road is shut on any paper, none of the three copies is taken down or torn up, no hurdle is lifted, no bar is tried, nobody goes up that cart track, the ninth yard does not start, the mallet is not picked up, and the drawer at the back of that office is not opened.

**`state/continuity.md` 1799 and `state/open-threads.md` 761 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it:** four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure, a page in a woman's hand is not a cure, a sentence in an unclaimed hand on a folded sheet is not a cure, **a bleed that has not faded in ninety-two days is not a cure, and NINETY-TWO IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN FIGURE AT ITS LAST DATELINE AND IT IS THE SAME WARNING AND NOT A NEW ONE: the inherited warning prints the same clause at two hundred and sixty days, which is the volume's last page and not this block's, that figure is not withdrawn and is not superseded, and the two are the same claim at two datelines and a writer inherits both and quotes whichever belongs to the chapter he is on**, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, a gate coming off its hinges about nine hundred yards of a stair away is not a victory and a gate that is still held is not a defeat, being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down, and **a line with a trade on it is not a name and a paper nobody can seal is not a freedom.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 757 to 764, and to 756, 755, 754, 753, 752, 751, 750, 749, 747, 743 and to every clause of 745 to 719 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel.** The volume's one is reserved for Block 0003. **And these ten files print no panel-shaped paragraph about the bleed either, and it is not bold and not alone and not spoken aloud and nobody else knows.**
- **Do not print the antagonist's name once, and do not print the bare surname as a printing, and do not use either withdrawn reference of the kind that names him.**
- **Do not spend more than two names out of the volume's six, and do not leave the block's two unspent by accident.**
- **Do not fill the roll, put a name against any road, shut a road on the strength of any paper, take down any of the three copies, tear one up, or nail the new sheet over the roll.**
- **Do not go into the low room at the back of that office, do not open the drawer in it, do not name what is in it beyond what §4 of the outline already names, and do not ask anybody what a seal is for or what a gate is for.**
- **Do not conduct any of the three hand-offs.** No hurdle is lifted and no bar is tried up that shut track, **and a successor may not make the roadkeeper the one who tries it in this block either**, and nobody goes up that cart track a third time and nobody is shown standing behind all nine hurdles. **The sealed community sends nothing and is never asked, and nothing in this block implies where it is.**
- **Do not enter the Gatehouse, do not put anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair, and do not report anything out of it.** The occupation is a sheet on a board and about nine men with a warrant who are not in this county.
- **Do not open, close or cut any route, do not explain the mechanism, do not say what a roadmark is, do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says a person, and do not have any character notice the warmth of the left palm.**
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight.** The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not put the man of forty-one in a scene or ask him anything.** He says sixteen words in the whole of Volume 16 and is asked nothing here.
- **Do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill, the nine households on that mile of stone and orchard, or the nine who refused the roll into a body.** They are nine houses, nine households that voted, and nine people who said one thing each.
- **Do not ask anybody for an account of having said no, do not ask the roadkeeper or the woman of about twenty-nine about the broom straw, and do not ask anybody whether she wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not let the three answers of Volume 16 and the three answers of this block become one answer, do not resolve the incompatibility between any of them, and do not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or a fourth voice of any of them.**
- **Do not put the practice into the register, the day-book, under a fifth head, or onto this county's copy of the hand paper, and do not have the copyist rule a head.** Nothing about the practice is on any paper in this volume.
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration, do not print the word, do not put anything about the two of them in any document, do not let anybody else comment on it, and do not do this block's relationship work.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift or schedule the bar at the Low Gate, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, start the ninth yard of the wall, or pick the mallet up.**
- **Do not lift the cloth off the bench and do not have anybody ask what is under it.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not cure or explain the bleed or give it a panel.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll or who wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not merge the three series, derive one from another, change the band figure, or print it anywhere. Do not convert a path's count into main-world days, and do not month, weekday or tide a path mouth.**
- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth.**
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.** The word *failed* is not used about the shut road four hundred miles off and is not used about anything at all in this volume.

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0800, 0798, 0795, 0788 and 0783.** Read them before writing a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else. **The dateline line carries the weekday and the market and the state of the room over the weigh-house and about four more clauses, and this block's first dateline has the room open on it for the first time in this manuscript's memory and says so.**

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names **some of** the figures in the chapter that are not in it, being that the list is a list of examples and not a complete inventory and a successor may not print it as complete.
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED FILES ON DISK, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK WITH NO FREE VALUE IN IT AT ALL.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, **and every spelling means the hundreds that value prints under and to no other, being *one hundred* and *a hundred* in the one hundreds, *two hundred* in the two hundreds and *three hundred* in the three hundreds, each with the remainder written as *and* the tens or as the tens with no *and*, plus the bare digit with a non-digit on either side of it, with a chapter heading not read as a total, run over every file whole.** **RUN COMPLETE OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED FILES IT GIVES 284 PRINTED VALUES IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BAND, AND ZERO FREE ONES, AND NOTHING UNDER SIXTY IS FREE EITHER.** **THE INSTRUMENT HAS TO BE WRITTEN OUT EVERY TIME AND IT HAS FAILED TWICE IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and a writer who meets either withdrawn figure has to know which way it failed: too narrow, being an instrument that omits the *a hundred and …* spelling, returns values that are already printed, and that is how the withdrawn set of twelve came about, five of which are demonstrably printed; too wide, being an instrument that pairs every remainder with every hundred, counts *a hundred and sixty-six* as a printing of two hundred and sixty-six, and that is how the withdrawn figure of two hundred and eighty-four came about.** **AND THE CEILING OF THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS NOT LIFTED. Lifting it is an outline decision and `outline/volume-17.md` §7 has declined it on the page with three reasons and the third of them deciding, so this block's ten totals ARE REUSES AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT ALL TEN OF VOLUME 16'S LAST BLOCK'S CLOSING PARAGRAPHS NOW DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC**, in this form: the band from sixty to three hundred and forty-three has been searched whole again and three values in it are not a value any file in the manuscript before them has printed, being two hundred and sixty-six, two hundred and seventy-three and three hundred and twenty-six, and not one of the three can be used, because the over-figure of each of them is one of the barred six, and the ten totals of these ten columns are printed already, and the reason is arithmetic, and the route below sixty is shut, because ten distinct prices cannot sum under fifty-five and every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed and nothing under that is free either. **The barred six are 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41 and none of them may be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum. **THE FIGURES OF THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS ARE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE EIGHT-HUNDRED-FILE SET AND NOT AGAINST A CARRIED ONE, and if the rebuild returns zero usable free values, which it will, that is a correct answer and must not be reprinted with a withdrawn reason.**

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline. `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Volume 16's Batch 0003 drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, and the cheapest check is that Mudmonth is sixty days and every other month is thirty, so any day of month above thirty printed inside Mudmonth is wrong on sight, and this block is entirely outside Mudmonth.** The table at §3 already carries all of these per dateline and it was derived one by one.

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 89 at day 2970, Volume 16's last page, and 90 at day 2971.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, **and a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count.**
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 624 at day 2971 and 665 at day 3012.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 391 at day 2971 and 432 at day 3012, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 343 days ago at day 2971 and 384 at day 3012, and the road has been shut 324 days at day 2971 and 365 at day 3012.** Nobody goes up it in this block.

- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced, **and it is two hundred and sixty-five days past its date at day 2971 and three hundred and six at day 3012 and has shut nothing.** The roll was nailed up on day 2827 and is **one hundred and forty-four days on the boards at day 2971 and one hundred and eighty-five at day 3012, with nine empty lines on each of three copies and the fourth line empty on all three.**

Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
